title: Korean Armistice Agreement (1953)
key_facts: Ceasefire agreement signed on July 27, 1953, by the UN Command, North Korea, and China
Established the Korean Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) and a ceasefire line near the 38th parallel
Suspended hostilities but did not constitute a formal peace treaty
causes: Stalemate after major offensives and international pressure to end active combat
War-weariness and heavy casualties on all sides
Desire to stabilize the peninsula while broader Cold War tensions persisted
outcome: Cessation of active hostilities and prisoner exchanges
Creation of the Military Armistice Commission to supervise the ceasefire
Continued division of Korea without a formal peace settlement
impacts: Institutionalized the DMZ and long-term armistice regime
Shaped US and allied force posture in Northeast Asia
Left the Korean conflict unresolved, impacting diplomacy to present day
